quest.title: For Old Time's Sake
quest.description: Chang the Ninth of Qingce Village said he was going to Wuwang Hill in search of inspiration, but has yet to return. Granny Ruoxin is getting worried...

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: *sigh* Come home, Little Chang... You're starting to worry me...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who is Little Chang...?

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Oh... It's just my pet name for Chang the Ninth.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: I'm so used to calling him Little Chang now, it feels strange saying "Chang the Ninth."

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Last night, he said he was going out to do some research for his novel. I didn't think anything of it, just told him not to stay out too late. The usual.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: But he still hasn't come back. I'm so worried something's happened to him.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: And I'm too old and frail to go out looking for him. Could you two dears go and find him for me?

choices.text: Do you know which way he went?

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: *sigh* There's only one place he'll have gone. Wuwang Hill, north of here.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Please, go and find him — for my sake. He's been out there so long... I do hope nothing's happened to him.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Hmph! These wretched monsters... Ghastly things...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: All I wanted was one measly morsel of inspiration for my novel... But nope, I got stuck with this rabble instead!

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Thanks for your help. I'm not sure what I would have done without it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Granny Ruoxin is worried sick about you.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Is she? She's wasting her energy... I'm quite capable of looking after myself. I could have easily dealt with them if it came to it... It just would have been a bit of a bother, that's all...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: ...Still, I'm glad you showed up. Otherwise, I could have been here a while longer... This way, at least I won't have to put up with her constant nagging when I get back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...And just like that, he's gone. We should get going, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait — what's that on the ground? Did Chang the Ninth drop something?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We should take a look, just in case.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: *sigh* Oh, Little Chang...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Chang the Ninth is back, safe and sound.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Yes, I saw! Thank you, dears.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: He's always been this way, since he was a boy... Running off and getting himself into trouble, protesting that he's all grown up... He'll never grow up, though.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Anyway, it's nothing you should fret about. Little Chang will do as Little Chang pleases.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Thank you for going all that way to bring him home. Please accept this in return.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: I won't keep you any longer, I'm sure you have things to get back to. But... please don't end up like Little Chang. He's so preoccupied with how he's seen by others that he's never gotten round to taking a long, hard look at himself...

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Alas, mortals are no adepti... And what is mortal life but a short sufferance that comes before death? Alas!

talks.objective: Give the pages to Chang the Ninth

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: *sigh* I need to make this novel a good one... But how?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you drop these?

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Hmm? Oh... Yes, these are mine. But I didn't like what I'd written, so I scrapped them. Tossed them into the river.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: I can't believe you went and collected them all... This writing's barely legible now anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What were you writing?

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: A story for a girl I knew as a child. These are early drafts that I scrapped. Ah, that little girl... You've no idea what she was like when we were small. Constantly badgering me to read her a story.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Regrettably, I never had much time to write back then. I wrote the beginnings of a story to start her off, telling myself I'd write the rest when I had more time.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: And then one day, she disappeared. I couldn't find her anywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Hmph. It's because of her family, I'm sure of it. They never liked me, didn't want her to have anything to do with me. So they waited for an opportunity to quietly move out of Qingce Village for good.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Well, they'll soon see! Once I've made a name for myself they'll never look at me in the same way again! As soon as I've finished this story I'm writing for her, I'll see that it gets sold all over the world!

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: That way, they'll see the new me from wherever they are in the world! They'll see I'm not the same Chang the Ninth I was as a kid!

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: And then... And then I can see her again... But first things first — I need to actually get the story written.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: ...I—I'm sorry, look at me, giving you my whole life story! Anyway. I should get back to working on my book.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: *sigh* Come home, Little Chang... You're starting to worry me...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why did Chang the Ninth go to Wuwang Hill?

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: He said it was to do some research for his novel. It's nice and quite there, he says. Helps him get inspiration.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: But there's not a soul in Qingce Village who believes that's his real reason for going there.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Now, where was I up to...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's the girl's name?

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Why, what's it to you? ...Anyway, she preferred me not to use her full name — too formal, she'd say. So I called her by her nickname.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: But... she'll be all grown up after this many years. I don't think the nickname would suit her anymore...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: If I see her again, I'll have to use her full name... But anyway, forget it. I'm not telling you her name — full, nick, or otherwise.
